newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZAMBIA SAYS WILL RECORD FOOD SURPLUS IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA SAYS WILL RECORD FOOD SURPLUS IN 1997.

text.p: Zambia will record a food surplus in 1997, but a shortage of fertiliser and late rains will keep the maize harvest below last year's bumper levels, the ministry of agriculture said on Friday.
The ministry forecast a maize crop of 15.3 million 90kg bags against a national consumption of around 12.5 million bags.
The harvest would, however, be 2.13 percent lower than the 15.7 million bags harvested last season.
"The reason for the decrease in maize production could be attributed to non-availability of fertiliser and the discontent among some farmers over past marketing problems," a ministry spokesman said.
The late distribution of some fertilisers and prolonged rains would also play a role.
"Continious rains in January and February, resulting in leaching, logging and flooding in some parts of the country may erode some of the positive impact of seed," the spokesman said.
